events.text: Velvet cloak restoration concerns the faded green cloak from our fictional production The Lantern Gate. Stabilize the lining before attempting surface cleaning. The traveling costume crate will be refitted separately; this restoration notebook follows the garment itself.

Tour costume crate refit: replace the cracked inner rails and add a removable garment bar. The route has four stops, but transport planning is outside this file. We will measure the cloak after the restoration team has stabilized it.

Restoration dye test, swatch C. The velvet cloak restoration team recorded a copper fringe after the test dried overnight. This sample was rejected for treatment, but its card should remain in the experiment record. No dye was applied to the cloak.

Velvet cloak restoration and tour costume crate refit share this hanging trial. The stabilized cloak needs a padded bar with a 38 cm clear drop below it. Measure the crate with its lid shut, keeping the original hanger as a labeled comparison.

Packing slip fragment: two soft sleeves, seven brass pins, green mark. The customer name has torn off. The slip could belong to the cloak work or to a different delivery; none of the remaining handwriting resolves that uncertainty.

Conservation lecture handout saved as background for the velvet cloak restoration. Historic velvets can lose pile when brushed against the nap. These examples are from a teaching collection, and the handout does not prescribe a treatment for our cloak.

Tour costume crate refit inspection: the removable bar now clears the closed lid by 12 mm. Keep the old rails with the workshop scrap until the final fit is accepted. These measurements were taken on the empty crate this morning.

Velvet cloak restoration care card: support the hem on a folded cotton sling during inspection. We selected the sling after a dry fit; the lining stitches have not yet been tested under travel vibration. Keep the garment flat between sessions.

Household sewing reminder: replace the missing button on my raincoat before the weekend walk. The thread is in the kitchen drawer beside the spare shoelaces. This is personal mending and has no connection to the theater's costume work.
